Donald Trump met his two favorite authoritarian leaders this week for a
[historic trilateral
summit](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/11/18/trump-xi-putin-
meet-with-conflicting-agendas-sharp-divides/) that, of course, produced no
breakthroughs on the major issues currently facing the world. What it did
produce was Trump's glowing reviews of his "friends" [Xi
Jinping](https://www.facebook.com/washingtonpost/posts/youre-my-friend-and-we-
have-a-very-special-relationship-president-trump-said-of-/1515092737149263/)
and [Vladimir Putin](https://time.com/article/2026/11/19/trump-calls-putin-
friend-european-response-tusk-ukraine-war/) and [awkward photo
ops](https://www.thedailybeast.com/trump-smirks-at-putin-in-awkward-staged-
photo-with-dictators).

Meanwhile, at home, his [Cabinet's incompetence](https://zeteo.com/p/now-we-
know-what-stands-between-trumps) was on full display as his administration
struggled to calm concerns after a series of outages hit the country's cyber
infrastructure, including at the [National Security
Agency](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/national-security-agency-network-outage-
software-vulnerability/). Trump's reaction was also less than reassuring:
"[It's life](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/trump-downplays-
bank-email-travel-outages-faa-ground-stop-microsoft-rcna609796)."

Indeed, so goes life in Trump's America, where the DOJ is sending threatening
letters to Democratic lawmakers, ICE is detaining green card holders, and the
White House is challenging requests to preserve documents. Here's more on how
Trump and his cronies harmed democracy, undermined the Constitution, and hurt
societies worldwide this week:

#### **Saturday, Nov. 14 - Judge Blocks Trump's Massive Golf Course
Renovation**

A federal judge [temporarily
blocked](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/14/judge-rejects-trumps-bid-to-
immediately-close-east-potomac-golf-course-01166639) the Trump
administration's closure of the East Potomac Park golf course for a massive
renovation, calling the Park Service's insistence that the park needed to
close by Sunday "irrational" and finding that the rush to close the park was
an effort to fulfill orders from the president.

The decision came one day after the judge
[warned](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/14/us/politics/trump-east-potomac-
golf-course.html) she would begin contempt-of-court proceedings if she learned
that the Interior Department violated her court orders to preserve documents
related to the case. Whistleblowers had recently
[warned](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/10/politics/trump-building-investigation-
democrats-house-natural-resources) that key paperwork relating to Trump's
construction projects had already been destroyed.

#### **Sunday, Nov. 15 - Trump's DOJ Sends Threatening Letters to Dem
Lawmakers**

Trump's Justice Department
[sent](https://x.com/USAttyReitz/status/2121943768345780568) a threatening
letter to Senator Elizabeth Warren warning of "significant legal consequences"
over her recent comments about possible investigations she may pursue as the
expected Senate Banking Committee chair in the next Congress.

The letter suggested Warren "intend[s] to target private individuals close to
President Trump" and ordered her to preserve materials "relevant to your
intent to weaponize congressional investigations and deprive citizens of their
core constitutional rights."

Trump's DOJ later sent similar letters to Senator [Adam
Schiff](https://x.com/USAttyReitz/status/2123008320059666588) and Reps.
[Robert Garcia](https://x.com/USAttyReitz/status/2122456185177882744) and
[Jamie Raskin](https://x.com/USAttyReitz/status/2123378251498205559).

#### **Monday, Nov. 16 - Trump Goes on Racist Rant Against Black Journalist**

While speaking to reporters, Trump [lashed
out](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2122388455959535623) and made racist remarks
against NBC White House correspondent Yamiche Alcindor, calling her "pathetic"
and saying, "I know you don't see dirt," and "you'd never notice broken
windows, obviously, from where you come."

Trump's comments came after Alcindor asked him to respond to criticism that he
was too focused on D.C. construction projects during the nationwide ground
stop last week.

#### **Tuesday, Nov. 17 - ICE Detaining Green Card Holders**

The _Washington Post_
[reported](https://www.washingtonpost.com/immigration/2026/11/17/they-had-
green-cards-years-then-they-were-detained-by-ice/) that ICE is detaining green
card holders for minor violations that in some cases occurred decades ago.

The detentions are taking place despite the fact that the charges didn't even
come up when applying for or renewing green cards, and would typically result
in a citation rather than an effort to eliminate someone's legal status in the
U.S.

#### **Wednesday, Nov. 18 - White House Challenges Records Requests**

White House counsel Will Scharf [addressed](https://thehill.com/wp-
content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/Ranking-Member-Request_11.18.26.pdf) a letter
to congressional Democrats arguing the Trump administration isn't required to
comply with any requests or demands to preserve documents or information.
Scharf also ridiculously claimed in the letter, which
[reportedly](https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/6228627-white-house-
will-scharf-democrats-oversight-trump-administration-probes/) wasn't sent to
committee leaders, that Democratic lawmakers "may inappropriately seek to use
oversight investigations to harass individuals with meritless claims."

Scharf's letter came after incoming House Oversight Chair Robert Garcia
[sent](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/18/g-s1-154147/robert-garcia-house-
democrats-investigations-trump-administration) letters of his own to Trump
administration officials, allies, and family members, warning them to save
their records for upcoming investigations.

#### **Thursday, Nov. 19 - ICE Pays AT&T For Call Records**

404 Media [reported](https://www.404media.co/ice-is-paying-at-t-to-dig-
through-a-mountain-of-call-records-hemisphere-data-analytical-services/) that
ICE has paid telecoms giant AT&T millions of dollars to access its "raw data
and analytical services" to help with the agency's investigations.

The agreement has caused controversy for civil liberty experts, who say the
data-sharing represents a mass surveillance program - one that could provide
ICE with trillions of phone records, including those of non-AT&T customers.

#### **Friday, Nov. 20 - Watchdog Agency Abandoned Fraud Probe of Trump's
Memecoin**

The _New York Times_
[reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/20/us/politics/cftc-cryptocurrency-
trump-memecoin.html) that career officials at the Commodity Futures Trading
Commission opened an investigation into possible fraud related to Trump's
memecoin shortly after its launch in early 2025. They quickly abandoned the
inquiry, believing the commission wouldn't cooperate with the investigation,
including approving subpoenas.

In 2025 alone, Trump banked at least $636 million in transaction and licensing
fees associated with the cryptocurrency, while nearly a million buyers lost
[nearly $4 billion](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/04/us/politics/trump-coin-
crypto-investors-loss.html) through June 2026.
